product.description: Criza economică mondială are urmări și în Cairo. Multe afaceri s-au închis, multe prăvălii au dispărut. Ahmad Abd el-Gawad are de înfruntat un dușman mult mai necruțător: trecerea timpului. Vremurile petrecerilor nesfârșite au apus. Este țintuit la pat de boală, iar vechii lui prieteni se sting rând pe rând. Fiii și fiicele sunt și ei trecuți de prima tinerețe, fiecare cu împlinirile, dar și cu durerile sale. Kamal se vede la vârsta întrebărilor legate de sensul vieții, de comparația între aspirații și realizări. Nepoții întruchipează tânăra generație egipteană a deceniilor ’30–’40: unul dintre ei își construiește o carieră de înalt funcționar de stat; altul activează în rândurile Fraților Musulmani; cel de-al treilea este comunist și visează la revoluție. Și peste toate acestea, vine al Doilea Război Mondial. Neutralitatea formală a țării nu scutește orașul Cairo de spaima și ravagiile bombardamentului.   Mahfuz aduce în Strada Zahărului politica Egiptului și a lumii din febra celui de-al Doilea Război Mondial. De la microuniversul familiei, al orașului, autorul trece la dramele războiului, iar micile certuri de familie din primele romane devin acum dezbateri politice care dau narațiunii un ritm mai vioi. Boston Globe

# Strada Zaharului: A Historical Saga of Cairo During World War II

Immerse yourself in *Strada Zaharului*, a powerful work of historical fiction by Litera, that captures the dramatic pulse of Cairo during one of the most turbulent periods in modern history. This novel expertly weaves together intimate family struggles with the sweeping geopolitical forces of the Second World War, offering readers a rich tapestry of human resilience against global turmoil.

## ð Synopsis: Life and Conflict in Colonial Egypt

*Strada Zaharului* transports readers to a Cairo grappling with change. The narrative begins amidst an economic crisis that strips away illusions, forcing characters to confront not just hardship, but the very passage of time itself.

The story follows individuals like Ahmad Abd el-Gawad, who faces more than just earthly strugglesâhe confronts mortality and the fading glamour of past eras. Across multiple generations, the novel explores the weight of expectation as young adults navigate dreams against painful realities. Kamal, for instance, grapples with profound questions about lifeâs meaning and the gap between personal aspirations and actual achievements.

### A Crossroads of Ideology

The backdrop is populated by a younger generation representing the tumultuous Egyptian youth of the 1930s to 1940s. We meet characters embodying diverse political paths: one building a career in state civil service, another drawing strength from the Muslim Brotherhood, and yet a third dreaming radical revolution through communism.

Into this delicate socio-political landscape arrives the shadow of World War II. Despite Egyptâs formal neutrality, Cairo cannot escape the pervasive fear and devastation brought by global conflict.

## ð From Family Drama to Global Stage

Mahfuz masterfully expands the scope of the story. What starts as a micro-universeâthe dynamics within a single family or neighborhoodâgradually escalates into macro historical drama. The small, personal disagreements find themselves transformed into intense political debates, lending a vital and electric rhythm to the narrative. *Strada Zaharului* is not just a story of war; it is a profound study of how individual lives bend, break, and survive the overwhelming pressure of history itself.

### Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

**What genre is Strada Zaharului?**
This book falls under historical fiction (*Fictiune*), blending elements of family saga, political drama, and war literature.

**When and where does the story take place?**
The novel is largely set in Cairo, Egypt, primarily during the turbulent period leading up to and encompassing World War II (the 1930sâ1940s).

**Is this book suitable for history enthusiasts?**
Yes. The detailed portrayal of Egyptian political life, the rise of various ideologies, and the specific historical context of WWII make it highly engaging for readers interested in global history and culture.
